title: Effects of biotechnology on biodiversity
log: 2026-10-27T00:53:12Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Biotechnology and biodiversity
card: Genetic diversity is the variety of alleles in a population. It gives a species a better chance that some individuals will survive a change, such as a new disease.
Selective breeding picks a few individuals with wanted traits to breed. Genetic engineering can spread one modified gene through a whole crop. Both can mean fewer different alleles are used.
Farmers often grow one high-yield variety, or breed livestock from a few top animals. Individuals then become very alike genetically, so genetic diversity in the crop or herd can narrow.
If a new disease appears, a population with little variation may have no resistant individuals. Many can be affected at once, so the crop or herd is more vulnerable.
draft.remember: Less genetic variation means fewer chances that some individuals survive a new disease.

a.q: Why can growing one genetically uniform crop variety make a farm more vulnerable to a new disease?
opts: Few or no plants may carry alleles for resistance
The disease causes new mutations in every plant
Uniform plants cannot reproduce on their own
Uniform plants always grow more slowly than others
a.why: If all plants have nearly the same alleles, a disease that can infect one can infect them all, and there may be no resistant plants to survive and breed. The disease does not need to cause mutations. Uniformity does not stop plants reproducing.
a.clue: Think about whether any plant would be different enough to survive.

b.q: A dairy farmer in Gippsland breeds all her cows from two bulls with excellent milk yields. Which is the most likely long-term effect on her herd?
opts: Lower genetic diversity, so more risk from a new disease
Higher genetic diversity, because the bulls are healthy
No change, because selective breeding adds no new traits
Immunity to all diseases, because the bulls are strong
b.why: Using only two bulls means the calves share a small set of alleles, so genetic diversity can fall. A new disease could then affect many cows at once. High yield does not mean disease resistance, and a healthy bull does not add variety.
b.clue: Count how many different parents the herd comes from.

a.best: Few or no plants may carry alleles for resistance

b.best: Lower genetic diversity, so more risk from a new disease
